target_customer: Startups and small employers paying for employees' own consumer subscriptions as perks
problem: Employers spend on office perks few employees use. Cherry let employees pick services such as Netflix, Spotify or ClassPass and the employer paid for them.
business_model: B2B subscription, TechCrunch reported $149 per month for the first 10 employees and $15 or more per employee per month
product_category: Employee perks and benefits marketplace delivered through Slack

founders.name: Gillian O'Brien
founders.background_notes: Her own account says she was a first time founder with no tech industry connection before Cherry. Later roles at Dover, Pilot and Remote per the YC page.

founders.name: Emily O'Brien
founders.background_notes: Listed as founder and CTO on the YC page. TechCrunch calls the two founders sisters.

exit.reason: Seed raise during COVID was unsuccessful, so the founders wound the company down and aimed to return money to investors

competitors.name: AnyPerk
competitors.what: Employee perks and discounts platform for companies
competitors.traction_then: Raised $8.5M Series A in 2015, total about $13M

technical_complexity.rationale: A Slackbot plus gift code purchasing from subscription services. TechCrunch describes a Slack based marketplace of 40 plus services, which is standard integration work.

defensibility.rationale: Buying consumer subscription codes for employees had no technical or data barrier and relied on partnerships and a Slack distribution channel.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows an incumbent copying or buying Cherry. Cherry closed in 2021.

market_need_then: Cherry's own launch material says companies waste spend on perks nobody uses. The founders reported 88 percent engagement against a historical 7 percent for perks, a company claim.

identity.visual_style: Playful consumer look, not documented in detail
identity.voice_and_tone: Casual, startup friendly tone in TechCrunch coverage

branding.brand_signature: Slackmojis by Cherry, a free Slack emoji pack, plus a Perk Generator launched on Product Hunt
branding.community_and_virality: Product Hunt launches and Medium posts by the founders, no evidence of wide virality

brand_strength.rationale: Founder content and Product Hunt activity show effort, but no source shows press or community about the brand itself. The name is shared with a 2012 car wash startup and a German keyboard maker.

outcome_analysis: Cherry reached 40 or more paying customers after YC and raised an angel round of more than $700k, but a seed raise during COVID failed and the founders chose a planned wind down in early 2021. The founders said they were first time founders without industry context, and the team of two had limited runway, so the product never reached the scale a seed investor wanted.
notes: The $700k figure is stated as 700k plus in one Pilot blog post and the investors and date are not given. Pilot is the founder's later employer. Sources disagree on the Medium blog date of the shutdown post. Competitor search found Perkbox and others only on undated vendor pages, so they are excluded. startcherry.com returned HTTP 503 so the site is unverified.
